title: Same job, Riverhead and neighbouring towns
method: For each job title Riverhead and a neighbouring town both fill, the median, lowest and highest annual salary in each town's own salary record, in 2022, 2024 and 2026. Titles are matched by name; a few offices with different names are paired (Councilman and Town Council, Receiver of Taxes and Tax Receiver, Riverhead's Detective grades and Southampton's Detective, Southampton's numbered Police Officer steps). A median reflects who holds the title (how many are new or senior), not only the pay scale. Salaries only: no benefits, overtime, longevity or stipends. Southampton's vacant positions are left out. Real change carries the start-year median forward by the New York-area CPI-U.
caveats: Southampton's 2018 and 2020 salary charts are no longer on its website, so 2022 is the earliest year all three towns can be compared.
Southold's 2022 budget is not on its website; its start point is the 2021 Preliminary Budget.
Southold publishes salaries only for elected and appointed officials, so it appears only for elected offices.
Southampton has one appointed Sole Assessor; Riverhead and Southold elect three assessors. Southampton's Assessor is not compared.
Riverhead's Assessor figures leave out the chairperson, whose salary includes the chair's added pay.
Riverhead's January 2026 salary resolutions list no Town Clerk salary, so Town Clerk is not compared.
A Police Officer median mixes every step from recruit to top step, so it moves with hiring: Southampton's fell from 2022 to 2024 as new officers joined.
